A1.justification: Both ten-page PDFs describe the same SimLTD work. Their text, equations, algorithm, tables, figures, and references support reliable comparison after visual inspection. Neither supplied PDF contains an appendix.

before.justification: v1 reports original SimLTD results on LVIS and Objects365, transfer-learning experiments, and component and sampling ablations.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and reports additional supervised and semi-supervised results with Swin backbones.

M1.justification: The three training stages, frozen-feature transfer, head-tail fusion, augmentations, and losses remain unchanged in Sections 3.2–3.4 and Algorithm 1. Swin extends the evaluated configurations without a described adaptation to the SimLTD procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions retain LVIS v1 and Objects365 evaluation, the COCO transfer study, and COCO/Objects365 unlabeled sources. The added Swin experiments extend model configurations; the ImageNet pretraining disclosure does not introduce a new detection dataset, task, or domain.

E2.justification: Table 2 removes BAGS, ECM, and LogN and adds DiffusionDet. Figure 1 adds DiffusionDet, CascadeMatch, and MosaicOS to its plotted comparison and removes ECM. Most principal comparators remain; additional RichSem backbone variants retain the same comparison method.

E3.justification: Table 2 substantially extends the ResNet-based evaluation with DINO using Swin-T, Swin-B, and Swin-L under both supervised and semi-supervised settings. Existing splits, metrics, augmentations, and sampling protocols remain. Section 4.2 changes pretraining from 540K iterations for most models to up to 540K, without establishing that retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Figure 6 revises predicted boxes and class labels on the same four low-shot validation examples, changing the qualitative case-study evidence. The quantitative component, transfer-learning, and shot-count analyses in Table 4 and Figures 4, 5, and 8 remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Section 4.1 retains three differently seeded samples of Dk and reporting of averaged metrics. Neither version reports additional uncertainty intervals or significance tests.

E6.justification: Table 2 adds substantial Swin results, including supervised mAPbox of 41.1/47.2/49.8 and MixPL results of 42.5/49.0/51.5 for T/B/L. These are new configurations, not same-setting gains. Retained R50 MixPL rows also change: COCO mAPbox/APr moves from 37.7/32.4 to 38.5/31.6, and Objects365 from 37.2/31.2 to 38.3/30.8. Several GPU-hour values change, while Objects365 benchmark and quantitative ablation results remain.

T1.justification: Dataset partitions, formal conditions, and Equations 1–2 retain their mathematical content. Changing Dlt to Dltd is notation only; neither version contains formal theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the claims of simple three-stage learning, optional unlabeled supervision, scalability, and state-of-the-art LVIS performance. Scalability was already claimed in v1.

C2.justification: Section 4.4 qualifies the earlier general statement of outperforming RichSem as better performance with ResNet and comparable performance with Swin. Section 4.3 removes the explicit caveat about heterogeneous comparison protocols. The mechanism explanations and copy-paste overfitting caution remain.

D1.justification: Table 2 newly identifies ImageNet-1K/22K pretraining for ResNet/Swin and attributes Detic results to RichSem. Reported compute costs are revised, including R101 Deformable DETR from 124 to 234 GPU hours. Section 4.2 replaces submitted-code wording with open-source-code wording, but provides no code URL.

R1.justification: The references add DiffusionDet and Swin Transformer and remove BAGS, ECM, and LogN. Figure 1 refines positioning by supervision modality and training stages. The substantive related-work narrative and main novelty positioning otherwise remain.

P1.justification: The abstract receives localized rewriting, Sections 3.4 and 4.2–4.3 are condensed, and terminology and notation are polished. The section order and overall narrative structure remain intact.

P2.justification: Figure 1 receives revised axes, markers, and a six-category legend; Table 2 gains backbone comparison blocks; Figure 6 receives updated detection overlays. Other changes include highlighting and figure annotations. These modify existing displays while retaining the overall two-column layout and figure/table organization.

improvement.justification: Table 2 strengthens the evidence for scalability beyond v1's ResNet experiments, while pretraining provenance and the qualified RichSem discussion improve transparency. These provide a limited net improvement. Removing three baselines reduces comparison breadth, and the revised R50 scores and compute costs remain unexplained; the core method and quantitative ablations are otherwise unchanged.
